prompt: What is the first axial mode between two parallel walls 4.2 m apart? Take the speed of sound as 343 m/s.

options.explanation:
Correct. The speed of sound divided by twice the spacing: 343 ÷ 8.4 ≈ 40.8 Hz.

```formula
f_1 = c / (2L)
f_1 = 343 / (2 × 4.2) ≈ 40.8 Hz
where
f_1: the first axial mode, in hertz (Hz)
c: the speed of sound in air, 343 metres per second (m/s)
L: the distance between the walls, 4.2 metres (m)
Hz: hertz, cycles per second
In words: the first mode is the frequency whose half-wavelength exactly spans the gap.
```
This divides 343 by 4.2 instead of by twice 4.2 (8.4). That gives 81.7 Hz, which is the second mode.
This divides 343 by four times the spacing (16.8) instead of twice it.
This multiplies 343 by 4.2 instead of dividing; the result isn't even a frequency.

workedExample:
At the first mode, half a wavelength fits exactly between the walls. Higher modes are whole-number multiples.

```formula
f_n = nc / (2L)
f_1 = 1 × 343 / (2 × 4.2)
f_1 = 343 / 8.4 ≈ 40.8 Hz
f_2 = 2 × 40.8 ≈ 81.7 Hz
f_3 = 3 × 40.8 ≈ 122.5 Hz
where
f_n: the nth axial mode, in hertz (Hz)
n: the mode number, 1, 2, 3 …
f_1: the first mode, in hertz (Hz)
f_2: the second mode, in hertz (Hz)
f_3: the third mode, in hertz (Hz)
c: the speed of sound in air, 343 metres per second (m/s)
L: the wall spacing, 4.2 metres (m)
Hz: hertz, cycles per second
In words: halve the wavelength to fit the gap: 343 ÷ 8.4 gives the first mode, and its multiples give the rest.
```
